The fixed positional encodings are defined using **sine and cosine functions of different frequencies**:

\begin{aligned}
PE_{\text{pos},2i} &= \sin\!\left(\frac{\text{pos}}{10000^{\,2i/d_{\text{model}}}}\right),\\
PE_{\text{pos},2i+1} &= \cos\!\left(\frac{\text{pos}}{10000^{\,2i/d_{\text{model}}}}\right),
\end{aligned}
\]

where *pos* is the position and *i* indexes the dimension.

The retriever encodes each document \(z\) with a BERT‑based document encoder \(d(z)\) and encodes the query \(x\) with a BERT‑based query encoder \(q(x)\).  It then retrieves the top‑\(k\) documents whose dense representations have the largest inner product with the query representation – a Maximum Inner Product Search (MIPS) problem that can be solved approximately in sub‑linear time.  This approach is described in the DPR component of the model.

RAG‑Sequence uses **one retrieved document for the whole output sequence** – the same latent document is marginalised over to produce the probability of the entire sequence.

The Transformer injects token order by adding **positional encodings** to the input embeddings.  
These encodings are summed with the embeddings at the bottom of the encoder and decoder stacks.  
Because the embeddings and the positional encodings must be added element‑wise, the positional
encodings are required to have the same dimensionality as the model’s hidden size, \(d_{\text{model}}\) (e.g., 512 in the base model).  

[attention‑is‑all‑you‑need.pdf — Page 6]
